content.text:
1) Answer to the prompt

Claim: Manfred Weber values human rights.

Evidence:
- He backed disciplining a governing party inside his own political family over rule‑of‑law concerns. In March 2019, Weber supported suspending Hungary’s ruling Fidesz from the European People’s Party (EPP), a move explicitly linked to breaches of EU principles; in 2021 he said Fidesz’s stance on the rule of law made it “too problematic” to remain in the EPP group. These are costly, public positions to defend EU values, including fundamental rights. ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2019/03/20/german-conservatives-float-compromise-to-defuse-eu-row-with-hungarys-orban?utm_source=openai))
- He advocated tying EU money to respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law. In October 2020, Weber argued that access to the EU budget and recovery funds must be conditional on freedoms like media pluralism and separation of powers—i.e., the EU’s human‑rights architecture in practice. ([manfredweber.eu](https://manfredweber.eu/en/active-for-europe/the-respect-of-the-rule-of-law-must-be-a-condition-to-get-european-funds/?utm_source=openai))
- He consistently condemned authoritarian repression and backed democracy/human‑rights defenders abroad. Examples include: calling (with other group leaders) for new and free elections in Belarus and condemning torture and violence against peaceful protesters; warning against Lukashenka’s abuses and hybrid attacks; and supporting the democratic opposition (Sakharov context) in Belarus. ([eppgroup.eu](https://www.eppgroup.eu/newsroom/we-call-for-new-and-free-elections-in-belarus?utm_source=openai))
- He chose not to lend legitimacy to a regime accused of systematic abuses: in 2021, Weber announced the EPP Group would not take part in the European Parliament’s electoral mission to Venezuela so it would not be “interpreted as support” for Maduro’s regime, repeatedly condemned by the EP for human‑rights violations. ([eppgroup.eu](https://www.eppgroup.eu/newsroom/epp-group-won-t-participate-in-mission-to-venezuela?utm_source=openai))
- He treats privacy/data protection as a fundamental right to be safeguarded at EU level, praising the EU data‑protection settlement as a balance that protects Europeans’ privacy—another core rights domain. ([eppgroup.eu](https://www.eppgroup.eu/newsroom/eu-data-protection-agreement-strikes-the-right-balance-says-epp-group-chairman-manfred-weber?utm_source=openai))
- He ties European security policy to defence of freedom and rights, pushing sanctions against Russia for aggression and rights abuses, and publicly stating Putin “has no interest to stop the war,” while aligning with transatlantic sanctions to defend Europe’s “way of life.” ([reutersconnect.com](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/we-are-stronger-now-germanys-weber-says-after-trumps-sanctions-on-russia/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjU6bmV3c21sX1ZBNTg2MzIyMTAyMDI1UlAx?utm_source=openai))

Conclusion: Over more than a decade, Weber’s leadership decisions, policy positions (rule‑of‑law conditionality, privacy), and external‑relations stances (Belarus, Venezuela, Russia/Ukraine) show a consistent pattern of prioritising human rights and the rule of law—even when politically costly within his own camp. The preponderance of actions and statements supports the claim that he values human rights. ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2019/03/20/german-conservatives-float-compromise-to-defuse-eu-row-with-hungarys-orban?utm_source=openai))

  [1] Reasoning 1: DW is Germany’s international public broadcaster, generally reliable with transparent sourcing.
